I am 76 years old. My legs ache in the cold mornings but I know this land. My father farmed it, I farmed it, and I will farm it until I cannot. I have 5 mu of contracted land here in Quzhou. There is really only one question I ask at the start of each year: wheat then corn, same as always. That is what this land is for. That is what everyone does here. I do not need to think hard about this.

For wheat, I will plant in October. I buy improved seed — Jimai variety — from the village supply station. I have used it before, it works. I will ask the tractor man to come rotary-till my field before sowing. I cannot manage the ploughing myself anymore. I will spread compound fertilizer before planting, then top-dress with urea when the stalks are shooting up in spring. I irrigate three times: once before the winter cold sets in, once when it joints, once when the heads are filling. I spray herbicide once after the seedlings emerge and spray again in spring for aphids if I see them. I expect around 400 jin per mu — not the best but enough.

After wheat harvest in June, I go straight into corn. I plant Xianyu hybrid seed, same kind I bought last two years. No need to till again — the soil is still loose. Just direct seeding. I put down some urea when the corn is knee-high. Rain is usually enough in summer but if it turns dry I will run one irrigation. I spray herbicide once early. By September it is done.

I will not try anything new this year. I am 76. New methods need young eyes and strong backs. I just need the harvest to cover my expenses and leave a little over.
